items.title: Grab, govt join forces on RM160mil gig worker welfare package
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Grab Malaysia is working with the government to co-fund a RM160 million package aimed at boosting gig workers' earnings, reducing operating costs and strengthening social protection. To boost earnings, the government and Grab have proposed minimum baseline rates for e-hailing and p-hailing workers, with adjustments expected to take effect in 2027. Grab said the proposed rates would increase workers' take-home earnings while keeping passenger fares stable during the implementation of the framework.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Fomca welcomes education funding, flags rising school costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) has welcomed the substantial allocation for education under the 2027 Budget, but cautioned that parents continue to face rising school-related expenses. Its chief executive officer Dr Saravanan Thambirajah said Fomca welcomed investments in school infrastructure, repairs to dilapidated schools, maintenance, early schooling assistance and supplementary food programmes. On higher education, technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and youth employment, he said Fomca supported initiatives to assist National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers, expand TVET and create more jobs for young Malaysians.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Mah Sing hails measures to boost housing affordability
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mah Sing Group Bhd welcomed the 2027 Budget measures to ease living costs and improve housing affordability by boosting household disposable income, reducing upfront homebuying costs and widening access to housing financing. "These initiatives are particularly timely in supporting first-time homebuyers and middle-income households, while providing positive momentum for Malaysia's residential property market," said Mah Sing founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum. Leong said the group particularly welcomed the proposed extension and expansion of stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers.

items.title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy. In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year. In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Lam Thye: Ensure swift compensation for accident victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Victims of accidents caused by drunk or drug-impaired drivers should receive fair compensation without having to endure lengthy court proceedings, says Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye. He welcomed the government's proposal to amend the Road Transport Act to make compensation mandatory for victims of accidents involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs. However, Lee said the government must establish a clear mechanism to determine the amount of compensation payable to victims.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet. Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction. Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.

items.title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said. MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.

items.title: MEF: June 2027 wage hike gives businesses breathing room
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed the decision to give employers until June 2027 to prepare for the minimum wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month. MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the transition period would give businesses time to plan while minimising disruption to employment and operations. Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy must consider not only higher salaries but also businesses' ability to sustain wage increases, retain existing workers and create new jobs.

items.title: Azalina: Law Reform Commission to address gaps in legal framework
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said in welcoming the announcement under the 2027 Budget , said it was a reflection of the government's continued commitment to legal and institutional reforms. She said the proposed commission would help identify outdated legislation, address gaps in existing laws and modernise legislation governing contracts, the sale of goods and mediation. She said institutional reforms required the government to be prepared to limit its own powers.

items.title: Haze disrupts routines, leaves parents scrambling for childcare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Worsening haze has disrupted daily routines, raised safety concerns among road users and forced parents to scramble for childcare arrangements following the short-notice announcement of school closures. While some have reported health concerns and cut back on outdoor activities, others are urging employers to consider work-from-home (WFH) arrangements to reduce exposure to the haze. Meanwhile, Nurul Adillah, who works in Cyberjaya, said she had stopped her usual outdoor activities as the haze worsened.

items.title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene. “The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.

items.title: PNB gets first new land endowment in over 40 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget will strengthen Permodalan Nasional Bhd's (PNB) mandate to grow Bumiputera wealth through a new endowment of 20.23 hectares of prime commercial land in Kuala Lumpur. PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said the allocation marks the group's first new endowment since its formative years in the early 1980s. He said it reinforces PNB's founding mandate to enhance Bumiputera wealth and participation through long-term value creation.

items.title: Tax relief could ease M40 burden, says consumer group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A prominent consumer group said 2027 Budget tax relief measures could ease the financial pressure on middle-income households amid rising living costs. Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan said the increase in individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000, alongside proposed tax rate reductions and wider deductions, would help M40 households manage their expenses. However, Fomca cautioned that tax relief alone would not fully address the financial challenges faced by the M40.

items.title: Four injured as 10-tonne lorry hits vehicles in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Four people were injured, including a man who sustained critical head injuries, when a 10-tonne lorry travelling against the flow of traffic rammed into vehicles in the opposite lane at the Alam Budiman traffic lights along Jalan Mokhtar Dahari today. "One of the men was trapped and sustained critical head injuries, while another man suffered abdominal injuries. A third man sustained minor injuries, while the woman suffered moderately critical head injuries.

items.title: 2027 Budget gives MoH room to push reforms, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the implementation of permanent appointments would take time, as the ministry needed to ensure candidates met the requirements and take into account the different batches and cohorts of medical officers. He said his ministry was working with the Higher Education Ministry, Public Service Department and Public Services Commission to address workforce issues more holistically. Asked whether the ministry planned to own helicopters for the FDS, he said the ministry's priority was providing healthcare services rather than operating helicopters.

items.title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million. MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk. Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.

items.title: 2027 Budget: MCMC to invest RM1bil in electronic medical records
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will invest RM1 billion to expand the Electronic Medical Record System to healthcare facilities nationwide. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said during the tabling of 2027 Budget that the government would introduce the MediAsas basic medical plan in January 2027 at an affordable premium. Meanwhile, electronic medical records will be expanded based on the principle of "one individual, one record" to improve transparency in private healthcare costs.

items.title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190. In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181). A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.

items.title: RM450mil opportunity for startups from Khazanah, KWAP - Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah's Jelawang Capital and the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) Pioneer Fund will invest RM450 million in start-up developments. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) Fund, KWAP's Dana Pemacu, and Khazanah's Malaysia Mid-Tier Companies (MTC) Fund - totalling RM2.1 billion - will also be utilised to strengthen mid-tier companies' capabilities in sectors such as electrical and electronics, digital, aerospace, and medical devices. "To attract private capital through equity crowdfunding (ECF) and peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms, RM270 million has been allocated to support small and medium enterprises (SMEs), mid-tier companies, and social enterprises.

items.title: 2027 Budget: RM5bil to strengthen internet connectivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will allocate RM5 billion to strengthen the country's internet connectivity through the Jendela project. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said WiFi coverage had been provided at all public university campuses, while 4G coverage had been extended to all Felda settlements. "We have so far successfully provided WiFi coverage at all public university campuses and 4G coverage in all Felda settlements," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget.

items.title: MARC: 2027 Budget balances growth with fiscal discipline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget reflects the government's sustained commitment to support economic growth while advancing fiscal consolidation, said Malaysian Rating Corp Bhd (MARC). Group chief executive officer Arshad Mohamed Ismail said the narrowing of the fiscal deficit, alongside sustained development expenditure, provides a foundation for strengthening Malaysia's economic resilience and long-term growth potential. He also welcomed the higher allocation for development expenditure at RM83 billion.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Govt allocates RM142mil to boost Nadi platform, online business
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will allocate RM142 million under 2027 Budget to strengthen the National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) platform and help more young entrepreneurs grow their businesses online. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the initiative would enable more entrepreneurs to tap into digital business opportunities and reach wider markets. The additional allocation is intended to help more entrepreneurs use digital platforms to promote their products, expand their customer base and grow their businesses.

items.title: Faster licensing to boost medical tourism, says APHM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Faster licensing of private healthcare facilities under a new online system could give Malaysia's medical tourism sector a boost, the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) said. He said the initiative was among the healthcare measures welcomed by APHM in the 2027 Budget, alongside efforts to strengthen public-private collaboration and improve patients' access to treatment. He said the measures could help reduce patient waiting times by making better use of private-sector healthcare capacity.

items.title: Penang welcomes 2027 Budget backing for proposed tech finance hub
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has welcomed the federal government's backing for its proposed Penang Technology Financial Centre (PTFC), saying the move would strengthen the state's technology ecosystem and support its push towards higher-value industries. He said the initiative would help Malaysia move towards a high-value, technology-driven economy while creating opportunities to strengthen local industries. "The state government submitted the PTFC White Paper to the Finance Ministry on Sept 23, and plans to submit the PTFC Strategic Blueprint and PTFC Action Plan by November," he said.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Prasarana to invest RM3.4bil in rail recovery programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prasarana Malaysia Bhd will invest RM3.4 billion in a rail service recovery programme to improve service reliability, operational efficiency and passenger experience under the 2027 Budget. In a statement, the public transport operator welcomed the measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, which emphasised accessibility, service reliability and passenger comfort. Prasarana said the investment formed part of its long-term commitment to strengthening rail system capacity and resilience, optimising asset performance and minimising service disruptions.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today. “With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said. Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups.

items.title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies. “This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.

items.title: Taxi, hire car and school bus drivers to get RM1,000 aid next week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Taxi, hire car and school bus drivers will receive a one-off RM1,000 financial aid following the sale of the special "H" number plate series, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced. He said the aid would benefit 38,000 taxi and hire car drivers and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide, with payments to be disbursed next week. "Following the recent sale of the special 'H' number plates, the government has agreed to give a one-off special financial aid of RM1,000 to 38,000 taxi drivers, including hire cars, and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.

items.title: 2027 Budget: One-off RM1,500 special aid for 1.3 million civil servants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has announced a one-off special financial assistance payment of RM1,500 for 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including contract workers. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said all government pensioners, including pensioned and non-pensioned veterans, would also receive RM750 in special financial assistance. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had agreed to provide a one-off special payment of RM750 to 70,000 KAFA religious teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks and other Islamic religious personnel.

items.title: Budget 2027: Form Six students to receive RM2,500 allowance, early school aid increases to RM200 per pupil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Form Six students will receive a RM2,500 cost-of-living allowance each next year, matching the rate given to matriculation students, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Speaking during the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament, Anwar said the assistance would benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide. Anwar also announced that the government would increase Bantuan Awal Persekolahan (BAP), or early schooling assistance, from RM150 to RM200 per pupil next year.

items.title: Saifuddin: 2027 Budget prioritises public safety, national sovereignty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM21.98 billion allocation to the Home Ministry under the 2027 Budget will strengthen security assets, border controls and technology to combat crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the allocation reflected the Madani government's commitment to safeguarding peace and public order, which he described as fundamental to national prosperity. Saifuddin said public welfare remained a priority, with investments in healthcare facilities, public transport assistance, skills development and employment opportunities.

items.title: Pasir Gudang tops nationwide API readings as 36 areas record unhealthy air
items.summary: In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 177 and Batu Muda 172, while Putrajaya recorded 170. Meanwhile, 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings. Up north, Penang's Balik Pulau recorded 89, Kedah's Kulim Hi-Tech recorded 85, Langkawi recorded 73, and Perlis' Kangar recorded 81.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Govt to disclose project contractors, contract values for transparency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will strengthen transparency by disclosing project information, including contractors and contract values, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. "With the Government Procurement Act coming into force in 2027, the government will strengthen transparency by disclosing project details, including contractors' names and contract values," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat. Anwar said the Madani reform agenda would continue to be strengthened "without fear" as the administration entered its fifth year.

items.title: Anwar brings poetry to 2027 Budget with Tamil, Chinese verses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Classical Tamil and Chinese poetry featured in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's 2027 Budget speech in the Dewan Rakyat today. Anwar, an avid reader of poetry, literature and political philosophy, including the works of Rumi, drew on the literary traditions of two ancient civilisations in his speech. Reciting the verse, Anwar said: "Thallaa Vilaiyulum Thakkaarum Thaazhvilaach Chelvarum Servadhu Naadu."

items.title: Permanent posts for contract doctors will help stem brain drain, says APHM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Offering permanent posts to doctors who complete their housemanship will help stem the brain drain and strengthen the country's healthcare workforce, said Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh. He said the move would give young doctors greater job security and clearer career prospects, encouraging them to build their careers in Malaysia instead of seeking better opportunities and stability abroad. "I am glad that the contract doctor issue is resolved and commend the government on offering permanent posts to doctors who complete their housemanship.

items.title: Budget 2027: Govt rolls out six initiatives to attract global firms, skilled talent
items.summary: Tabling Budget 2027, Anwar outlined six initiatives to improve Malaysia’s business environment and competitiveness, amid renewed investor confidence in recent years. Among other measures, Anwar said the existing Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive will be further improved starting January 2027. “New companies under the GSH incentive will enjoy a special five per cent tax rate on income from GSH activities.

items.title: Haze: Parents, students adapt to online learning as schools close
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prior experience with Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) has enabled parents and students to adapt smoothly as schools in several states closed due to haze. Teachers' prompt preparation of digital learning materials and assignments ensured uninterrupted education, allowing students to keep up with lessons and exam preparations at home. She praised teachers for quickly issuing assignment links and materials despite late-night closure announcements, making home instruction manageable for parents.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Govt mulls commission to overhaul outdated laws
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying a proposal to establish a Malaysian Law Reform Commission to review outdated laws and identify gaps in the country's legal framework. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also reviewing laws on contracts, the sale of goods and mediation to expedite the resolution of legal disputes. "The government is studying the establishment of a Malaysian Law Reform Commission to identify outdated laws and gaps in the legal framework.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government earmarks RM60m for Matrade, RM1b to boost MSME exports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 - The federal government will allocate RM60 million to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to help build local companies’ capacity to enter and diversify their overseas markets, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar said Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Berhad (BPMB) will also prepare RM1 billion to support local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to explore the export market. He said JOM Malaysia will also have RM10 million to bring rural products and high-value services to digital platforms and overseas markets.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Maternity leave up to 490 days, minimum pension RM1,350
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maternity leave entitlement for civil servants will increase from 360 days to 490 days throughout their service, while the minimum monthly pension will rise from RM1,000 to RM1,350 under the 2027 Budget. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said maternity leave would be increased to a maximum of 98 days per childbirth, with RM20 million allocated to improve childcare centres at government facilities. Meanwhile, he said the higher minimum pension would benefit nearly 59,000 retirees, armed forces veterans and derivative pension recipients.

items.title: One day to wedding, Syed Saddiq turns up for 2027 Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Most grooms spend the eve of their wedding making final preparations, but Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman had another date to keep today — attending Parliament. Dressed in a black Baju Melayu, Syed Saddiq attended the Dewan Rakyat for the tabling of the 2027 Budget, a day before his wedding to singer-actress Bella Astillah tomorrow. Two days ago, Syed Saddiq had said that the couple had to put their honeymoon plans on ice for now.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government halts public university disciplinary proceedings relating to free speech
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has halted disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly with immediate effect. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Higher Education Ministry was preparing a comprehensive legal framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), covering university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights. “With immediate effect, all disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly have been halted,” Anwar told the Parliament today during the tabling of the Budget 2027.

items.title: Anwar: Voluntary medical insurance MediAsas to kick off in 2027, EPF Akaun Sejahtera can pay premiums
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — MediAsas, a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan, will be launched nationwide at affordable prices in January 2027, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. While tabling Budget 2027 at Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said MediAsas would help keep hospital bills under control and more predictable according to diagnosis type. Anwar also said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributors under 55 years old can also tap into their Akaun Sejahtera to pay for MediAsas premiums.

items.title: Budget 2027: Duty‑free shopping limit in Langkawi and Labuan raised to RM10,000
items.summary: However, Anwar said visitors and tourists must stay for at least 48 hours to enjoy the higher duty-free shopping limit. “More locally made products from Langkawi will also be exempted from import duties to support local entrepreneurs,” he said. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said this when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Budget 2027: Higher Education Ministry gets RM19.1bil, RM800mil for university facilities upgrades
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Higher Education Ministry will receive RM19.1 billion under Budget 2027. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this will include RM800 million to upgrade university facilities and replace ageing equipment. A slight increase from the Budget 2026 allocation of 18.6 billion, the Budget 2027 allocation follows a broader expansion of the ministry’s responsibilities, with Form Six and matriculation students set to come under its purview from 2027, bringing pre-university education within the higher education system.

items.title: Budget 2027: Entertainment duty exemption for local film, theatre tickets in Federal Territories, creative sector gets RM130m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Tickets for local films and theatre performances in the Federal Territories will be fully exempt from entertainment duty starting in 2027, as part of the government’s efforts to support the local creative industry. The government will also strengthen the local animation ecosystem to develop 20 new intellectual properties (IPs) and commercialise Malaysian characters globally. The government also called on state administrations to introduce similar entertainment duty exemptions to support local creative practitioners.

items.title: Budget 2027: SMEs to gain up to RM6,000 each from income tax cuts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 300,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Malaysia are expected to have additional income of up to RM6,000 each amid expected lower taxes, as the federal government will be cutting their income tax rates, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. As a response to MSMEs’ concerns over rising operating costs, Anwar said the federal government has agreed to reduce their income tax rates by one percentage point: For the first RM150,000 in taxable income, the tax rate will be reduced to 14 per cent; For the taxable income from RM150,000 to RM600,000, the tax rate will be reduced to 16 per cent. Anwar said the government also proposes to extend the existing Accelerated Capital Allowance on capital expenditure for plant, machinery and ICT equipment for businesses until December 31, 2030.

items.title: Budget 2027: e-ART to be main urban public transport solution in Johor Bahru ahead of RTS Link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today said the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (e-ART) system would be the main solution for easing traffic congestion in Johor Bahru. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also add bus routes, increase bus and KTM Komuter service frequency, and provide Grab shuttle services in high-demand areas ahead of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link opening next year. “Traffic congestion in Johor Bahru must be addressed immediately.

items.title: Anwar: MA63 a national promise, 12 items finalised, more scholarships for Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: Referring to the agreement which was signed between the founding partners of Malaysia, Anwar said that 12 items under MA63 have been finalised so far, and also listed other measures and allocations that the federal government has been channelling to Sabah and Sarawak. Anwar said the federal government has agreed to increase Public Service Department (JPA) scholarship offers to Sabah and Sarawak’s students. Anwar said the proposed federal allocation for Sabah and Sarawak next year remains the highest, with Sabah to receive RM18.7 billion in 2027 (as compared to RM17.6 billion this year) and Sarawak to receive RM16.2 billion (as compared to RM15.1 billion).

items.title: Budget 2027: 9,000 contract doctors to be made permanent in 2027, incentive hike for paramedics and nurses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — More than 9,000 contract doctors will be given permanent posting in public healthcare facilities next year, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said the government has offered permanent positions for more than 15,000 contract doctors since 2023, including 4,000 doctors this year alone. “This means that after this, doctors who complete their housemanship will be offered permanent positions as medical officers,” Anwar said.

items.title: Budget 2027: Health Ministry allocation increased, RM1.2b earmarked for upgrading of public facilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry will receive RM47.7 billion next year, up from this year’s RM46.5 billion, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said RM1.2 billion will be distributed for repair, upgrade and maintenance works of all public hospitals and clinics. A total of nine new facilities, including a specialist clinic complex and daycare treatment centre at Hospital Sultanah Aminah in Johor, will also be constructed next year, Anwar said.

items.title: Budget 2027: School repair allocation doubles to RM2b, dilapidated schools get RM1.3b
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the Budget 2027 in Parliament, said the allocation increase would cover different types of schools, including national schools, Chinese and Tamil national-type schools, as well as registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools. “The allocation for national schools will increase to RM900 million, while Chinese national-type schools will receive RM100 million and Tamil national-type schools, RM50 million. “Registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools under the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim) will receive RM200 million, with the scope of funding expanded to cover their operating costs.

items.title: Budget 2027: Road Transport Act to be amended to require drunk, drug-impaired drivers to compensate victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Existing road transport law will be amended to make it mandatory for motorists driving under the influence to pay compensation to victims. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the amendments would cover driving under the influence of both alcohol and drugs under the Road Transport Act. Citing the crash, Anwar said such tragedies were deeply distressing and showed that road safety violations remained a concern despite tighter enforcement.

items.title: Chinese New Villages, non‑Muslim houses of worship to receive bigger allocations under Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today announced an increase in allocations for the maintenance of Chinese New Villages and non-Muslim houses of worship from 2027 onwards. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the allocation for infrastructure upgrades in Chinese New Villages will be increased to more than RM100 million, including repairs and rebuilding of ageing facilities. Separately, Anwar said the ongoing Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives have benefitted nearly 500 villages and 1,700 schools nationwide since 2024.

items.title: Budget 2027: Govt allocates RM80b for subsidies, STR and SARA rises to RM16b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government expects to spend more than RM80 billion on subsidies, assistance and incentives next year. “The government will also increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion next year, up from RM15 billion this year. Separately, the allocation for Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani will rise to RM750 million from RM630 million, with 35,000 sales events targeted next year.

items.title: Budget 2027: Relief for caregivers as service tax for older citizens’ care reduced, new tax exemptions and increased financial aid announced
items.summary: A full exemption will also be granted on care fees up to RM96,000 a year. Anwar said the government will also increase financial aid for senior citizens to RM1.3 billion next year, benefiting nearly 200,000 recipients. Two National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) will also be developed in Penang and Sarawak to support training, research and elderly care, Anwar said.

items.title: Budget 2027: All Malaysians to be automatically registered with EPF at 18
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — All Malaysian citizens will be automatically registered as members of the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) upon turning 18 to encourage earlier retirement savings, under a measure announced in Budget 2027. Currently, employees are automatically registered with the EPF when the fund receives their first employer contribution. The EPF is Malaysia’s main retirement savings fund, with contributions from employees and employers helping members build savings for their later years.

items.title: Budget 2027: DBKL to get RM400m for 120 acres of parks, walkways and upgraded facilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will be allocated RM400 million to create 120 acres of new green spaces and upgrade public facilities as part of efforts to make the capital more liveable. During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the plans include a 22km of covered pedestrian walkways linking landmarks such as the National Mosque, Dataran Merdeka and Central Market, as well as connecting public housing to schools, clinics and transport hubs. Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) was recognised for restoring Merdeka Stadium, with the National Stadium next in line.

items.title: Government allocates RM3.3b for rural infrastructure, RM2.5b to replace ageing water pipes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The allocation for rural road projects will be increased to RM2.3 billion, compared to RM1.3 billion in 2022. In his Budget speech today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that a total of RM3.3 billion will be allocated for rural basic infrastructure projects, including the installation of village streetlights, community facilities, and clean water and electricity supply. Access to clean water nationwide will continue to be improved through the National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) programme, with an allocation of RM2.5 billion.

items.title: Budget 2027: Stamp duty exemption proposed for first homes up to RM500,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has proposed a full stamp duty exemption on loan agreements and instruments of transfer for first homes priced up to RM500,000, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Anwar also said the government would provide a full exemption on the first RM500,000 and a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount for first homes priced up to RM750,000. “The exemption for abandoned housing projects will also take effect from January 1, 2027, to December 31, 2030,” he said.
